title: Canadian Sales Tax Guide for US SaaS Companies (2026 Update)
summary: Understand the Canadian GST/HST registration test for US SaaS sellers, normal vs. simplified registration, business customers, and separate provincial taxes.
body_markdown:
A US SaaS company can have Canadian GST/HST duties without a Canadian office. For a qualifying nonresident digital supplier, the simplified regime generally looks at more than CAD $30,000 of specified supplies to specified Canadian recipients over a twelve-month period.


That is a starting point, not a test based on all Canadian revenue. Customer registration status, platform sales, and whether you carry on business in Canada affect the result.


## Which GST/HST rules apply?


Use the[CRA's digital-economy registration guide](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/find-out-need-register.html) to classify the business before configuring billing.


Situation What to review


Nonresident digital seller not carrying on business in Canada Simplified digital-economy rules and the specified-supply threshold


Business carrying on business in Canada Normal GST/HST registration rules


Seller already registered under the normal regime Normal collection and reporting duties


Sales through a distribution platform Which party must collect for those sales


Sales to a customer registered under the normal regime The customer's status and evidence, especially under the simplified regime


Do not choose a regime solely because revenue is above or below CAD $1 million. That is not the general dividing line between normal and simplified registration.


## Normal vs. simplified registration


The[CRA registration page](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/register-gst-hst.html) gives the application paths and eligibility rules.


Under the simplified regime, a qualifying seller collects on covered supplies to specified Canadian recipients. It generally cannot claim input tax credits. Under normal registration, input tax credits may be available if the requirements are met.


These differences can matter if your business has Canadian costs or local activity. Review the[CRA's input tax credit rules](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/calculate-prepare-report/input-tax-credit.html) before treating tax paid as recoverable.


## Do you charge GST/HST to Canadian businesses?


“B2B” alone is not the answer. Under the simplified regime, the treatment differs when the customer provides evidence that it is registered under the normal GST/HST regime.


A business without that registration can still be a specified Canadian recipient. A normal-regime seller has different collection rules and should not apply a blanket B2B exclusion.


Collect and check the relevant registration details. Keep the evidence with the customer record rather than relying only on a company email address. The[CRA's digital-economy definitions](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/digital-economy-definitions.html) explain the terms used in this analysis.


## GST/HST is not the whole provincial review


HST combines federal and participating provincial components. Other provinces can have separate sales tax systems, including QST. For that review, use[Revenu Québec’s guidance for suppliers outside Québec](https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/consumption-taxes/gsthst-and-qst/special-cases-gsthst-and-qst/suppliers-outside-quebec/) .


A GST/HST registration does not by itself resolve every provincial obligation. Review where customers are located, what they buy, and the relevant province's rules. Do not use one nationwide rate for every customer.


## GST and HST rates by province


The following rates apply to ordinary taxable supplies once you have determined the place of supply and that you must collect. They do not include separate provincial sales taxes or QST.


Place of supply GST or HST


Ontario 13% HST


Nova Scotia 14% HST


New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island 15% HST


Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Québec, Saskatchewan, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Yukon 5% GST


Use the[CRA rate and place-of-supply guidance](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/charge-collect-place-supply.html) . A province's 5% GST entry does not mean that no provincial tax applies. Follow the[digital-economy location rules](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/charge-collect.html) for your regime and retain the location evidence; do not choose a rate from your US office address.


For an illustrative taxable CAD $100 subscription before tax, an Ontario supply has CAD $13 HST and a CAD $113 total. An Alberta supply has CAD $5 GST and a CAD $105 total. These examples assume collection is required and no exemption or other adjustment applies.


## Show the tax clearly on invoices


Make clear whether the advertised price includes tax or whether checkout adds it. The[CRA invoice guidance](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/charge-collect-which-rate.html) explains how to show the applicable rate and tax amount, or make clear that the total includes tax. Show HST as one combined tax rather than separate federal and provincial charges.


Keep the seller, customer, date, service period, description, amount, tax, and total in the billing record. Use the registration details required for your regime. A normal-regime customer's input-tax-credit documents can need additional details; do not treat a generic invoice template as the full legal checklist.


## How to prepare for registration


Build a file with:


- The seller's legal entity and business details.
- The product and how customers access it.
- Direct and platform sales, with dates and customer locations.
- Customer GST/HST status and supporting records.
- Canadian business activities and existing tax accounts.
- The proposed regime and effective date, with the reason for each.


Use the CRA application route for your facts. For nonresident normal registration questions, see the[CRA's nonresident enquiry process](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/corporate/contact-information/non-resident-gst-hst-enquiries/make-non-resident-gst-hst-enquiry.html) .


If you need help, compare providers using a written scope. Our[GST/HST registration provider guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/canadian-gst-hst-registration-providers) covers RSM Canada, BDO Canada, and direct registration.


## What changes in billing after registration?


Set the effective date, product treatment, customer location rules, and customer registration handling. Test a direct consumer sale, a registered business customer, a refund, and a platform sale before turning on collection.


Use a[SaaS invoice layout](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/invoicing-B2B-SaaS) that separates charges, tax, and credits, then check the fields required for your Canadian registration. Reconcile the tax report with invoices and credits each filing period. Keep platform-collected tax separate from tax you collected yourself.


## Filing, payment, and currency


Simplified GST/HST registrants file for calendar quarters, with the return due within one month of quarter-end:


Reporting period Standard return deadline


January–March April 30


April–June July 31


July–September October 31


October–December January 31


File through GST/HST NETFILE using the business number, reporting dates, and access code. Keep the confirmation. Normal-regime registrants follow their assigned reporting period; the simplified quarterly schedule is not a revenue-band choice. See the[CRA filing instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/file-return.html) .


Use the[CRA payment instructions](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/digital-economy-gsthst/remit-gst-hst.html) for the account and currency. Arrange payment separately when the filing route does not include it, and allow time for the funds to arrive.


A simplified registrant may request permission to file and pay in US dollars or euros. Wait for the CRA's designation and effective period before using that currency; a USD customer invoice alone does not authorize a USD return.


## Records and adjustments to keep


Retain sales by customer and province, customer registration checks, location evidence, invoices, payment records, tax calculations, platform reports, refunds, returns, and filing confirmations. Keep the exchange-rate source and calculation when you convert a transaction.


The CRA generally requires records for six years from the end of the last year to which they relate, and some circumstances require longer retention. Check its[business recordkeeping rules](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/keeping-records.html) .


Match a refund or credit to the original sale and the tax it carried. Preserve the original document and the adjustment so the customer record, tax report, and books agree. For app-store sales, establish who collected before reporting the same tax yourself; see the[Apple](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/apple-app-store-sales-tax-guide) and[Google Play](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/google-play-sales-tax-guide) guides.


Late filing and payment can lead to different penalties and interest. Use the[CRA penalty guidance](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/file-gst-hst-return/reporting-requirements-deadlines/gst-hst-filing-penalties.html) for the specific failure rather than a single estimated percentage.


## What if you should have registered earlier?


Reconstruct the sales history and establish the correct start date. Ask an adviser or the CRA about the registration and correction process for your facts. Turning tax on today does not settle prior periods.


Keep the facts and the conclusion in writing so future staff can understand why the account uses its current regime.
